evaluationScope: JDT LS, SootUp, and CodeQL evidence runs against first-class Quarkus and Spring Boot fixtures; framework and dynamic gaps remain explicit.

fixtures.role: Spring Boot framework fixture and entrypoint baseline

candidateSet.name: Eclipse JDT Language Server
strengths: Direct call hierarchy and source locations were verified against the Maven fixture.
Source-level interface, callback/lambda, generated-source, and ServiceLoader call sites were observed.
Maven project import and Java source navigation are already available through JDT/JDT LS.

gaps.impact: The source call to an injected interface is visible, but CDI bean selection, qualifiers, alternatives, producers, and Quarkus client proxies are not represented.
gaps.closure: Add Quarkus/Jandex and build-profile enrichment; map injection points to selected bean identities and normalize generated proxies.

gaps.impact: JDT LS does not create callers for HTTP routes, lifecycle callbacks, or container-owned @Bean methods.
gaps.closure: Add Spring/Quarkus framework models as a separate entrypoint evidence layer; keep external entrypoints distinct from Java source callers.

gaps.impact: The ServiceLoader call site is visible, but the concrete provider and classloader/module selection are not proven.
gaps.closure: Ingest META-INF/services and module-info provider declarations from the selected classpath; emit possible when provider selection is not unique.

gaps.impact: Generated calls resolve only when generated roots and the correct Maven profile are imported.
gaps.closure: Make source roots, effective classpath, profile, and generated-source fingerprints mandatory AnalysisContext inputs.

gaps.impact: Unconstrained Class.forName, Method.invoke, and Proxy targets are not represented as concrete incoming calls.
gaps.closure: Implement only bounded constant/configuration resolvers; retain unknown for arbitrary dynamic targets.
gaps.estimate: 4-7 engineer-days for constrained cases; no finite estimate for general resolution

gaps.impact: The probe evidence is not yet a production SemanticCallFacts adapter.
gaps.closure: Implement the provider boundary and normalize LSP results with certainty, provenance, and abstention fields.

candidateSet.closureEstimate: 20-33 engineer-days for a bounded MVP adapter, framework entrypoints, and enrichment; arbitrary dynamic Java remains intentionally unresolved.
candidateSet.decisionReason: Lowest initial integration risk and strongest source-level evidence, provided framework enrichment and abstention are explicit.

candidateSet.name: SootUp
strengths: Pinned CHA/RTA runs measured direct application calls, concrete callback implementations, ServiceLoader implementors, generated bytecode, and full Quarkus/Spring runtime classpaths.
The Quarkus runtime-scope CHA run completed with 118 dependency entries and 68 methods/59 calls; the FSI run used 104 entries and measured 6,224 methods/7,853 calls.
A library integration can avoid a long-lived language-server process and keeps the unresolved-edge policy under adapter control.

gaps.impact: CHA reaches concrete Quarkus and Spring implementations, but does not prove CDI/Spring bean selection, qualifiers, alternatives, producers, or framework proxy identity.
gaps.closure: Add the same Jandex/Quarkus enrichment layer and map bytecode proxy nodes back to application beans.

gaps.impact: Neither Quarkus REST nor Spring MVC, @Bean, and lifecycle entrypoints had incoming Java callers in the measured graphs.
gaps.closure: Add Spring/Quarkus route and lifecycle models and seed the call graph with explicit framework entrypoint nodes.

gaps.impact: The probe returns source lines and generated-class edges, but raw signatures and host paths require normalization before they satisfy SemanticCallFacts provenance.
gaps.closure: Keep the portable normalizer, validate line tables/source roots across profiles, and define stable method-signature normalization in the adapter.

gaps.impact: Reflection, ServiceLoader selection, and dynamic proxies remain open-world unless modeled outside the call graph.
gaps.closure: Add constrained metadata/configuration models and preserve unknown for unresolved targets.
gaps.estimate: 5-9 engineer-days for bounded cases; no finite estimate for general resolution

gaps.impact: The normalized spike output preserves evidence and certainty, but the library graph is not itself the required production SemanticCallFacts contract.
gaps.closure: Implement an adapter with graph scope, certainty mapping, source evidence, and coverage reporting.

candidateSet.closureEstimate: 22-38 engineer-days after the measured probe; includes adapter/provenance normalization, framework entrypoints, and enrichment. General dynamic resolution remains intentionally unresolved.
candidateSet.decisionReason: Runtime-scope CHA/RTA now passes on both the Java 21 Quarkus fixture and the external Spring Boot baseline; the remaining gaps are framework modeling, provenance adaptation, and intentionally unresolved dynamic behavior.

candidateSet.name: CodeQL for Java/Kotlin
strengths: A pinned Java database and query emitted 64 Quarkus facts and 2,356 FSI facts, with source locations and qualified caller/callee names.
The same query exposed direct calls, interface/callback source edges, generated-source calls, and explicit reflective/proxy API activity.
The query model can be extended with annotations and framework models while the normalizer preserves possible and unresolved outcomes.

gaps.impact: Both databases were created and queried, but --build-mode=none did not consume a compiled Maven build on macOS 27; test facts also require explicit scope filtering.
gaps.closure: Retain the pinned runner and buildless limitation, then add a supported compiled-build path or an equivalent dependency/profile import before production selection.

gaps.impact: The reverse-call query and portable normalizer emit measured source facts, but they do not yet provide a production query pack or all SemanticCallFacts relationship types.
gaps.closure: Extend the query/normalizer for framework facts, polymorphic candidate sets, stable signatures, and explicit coverage records.

gaps.impact: The measured query sees source annotations and interface calls, but CDI, Quarkus build-time beans, ServiceLoader providers, and framework proxies remain unmodeled.
gaps.closure: Build a small Quarkus model pack and compare its facts to the Jandex/context-based model.

gaps.impact: The measured query reports no incoming Java callers for Quarkus REST, Spring MVC, @Bean, or lifecycle methods; the new declarative framework contracts are not consumed by the provider run.
gaps.closure: Add Spring/Quarkus QL models or inject framework-entrypoint facts from AnalysisContext before querying reverse callers.

gaps.impact: General reflection and dynamic proxy target resolution remains difficult even with AST and call-graph predicates.
gaps.closure: Model only constrained configuration/constant cases and preserve unknown for open-world behavior.
gaps.estimate: 5-9 engineer-days for bounded cases; no finite estimate for general resolution

gaps.impact: The CLI/database/query process adds a process boundary, distribution dependency, and license/operational review for a service adapter.
gaps.closure: Define an isolated runner, query pack versioning, database cleanup, result transport, and operational limits.

candidateSet.closureEstimate: 26-45 engineer-days after the measured buildless database/query run; includes compiled-build or dependency-context support, query/fact normalization, framework entrypoints/models, dynamic abstention, and service integration.
candidateSet.decisionReason: The query engine produced useful, portable source facts, but buildless extraction and the process/query-pack boundary create the highest integration cost for a small reverse-call service.

selection.currentRecommendation: SootUp is the preferred technical foundation; JDT LS remains the lowest-risk source/compiler fallback, and CodeQL is a measured query-engine alternative with explicit buildless limits.
selection.notYetProven: No candidate is production-ready until it passes the mandatory acceptance criteria or has an explicit abstention and closure plan for every conditional/gap result. SootUp now has full runtime-classpath evidence but still needs the project-owned framework enrichment and SemanticCallFacts adapter.
nextEvidence: Implement the framework/context enrichment contract for CDI, Spring/Quarkus entrypoints, ServiceLoader, and generated proxies.
Compare the normalized facts, provenance completeness, setup cost, and unresolved-edge behavior before selecting the production adapter.
